verifiable.explanation: tests/test_decisions.py is a deterministic, programmatic scorer of /app/decisions.csv against baked labels; no LLM judge, no network, no runtime installs in test.sh (pytest and pytest-json-ctrf are pinned and baked in tests/Dockerfile). I reran the reference scoring twice and got byte-identical output.

solvable.explanation: solution/screen.py (stdlib only) runs in 3.2 s and scores recall 0.9849 / precision 0.9954 / uid 0.9992 with every per-class floor cleared (worst class T3_structure 0.9524 vs 0.90 floor; worst FPR R0 0.0012 vs 0.01). The 6 h expert estimate is credible for an 808-line rule engine.

difficult.explanation: Cross-script transliteration (Arabic/Persian/Cyrillic), stacked romanization conventions, Wade-Giles/Cantonese ambiguity, alias strength semantics and partial-DOB logic under simultaneous recall and precision floors is well beyond an undergraduate exercise; the decoy classes punish naive fuzzy matching.

interesting.explanation: Building and validating a sanctions screening engine against per-class recall/precision floors is literally the acceptance test a bank's model-validation function runs on a vendor engine. Real job, real money.

outcome_verified.explanation: Tests read only the final /app/decisions.csv and grade the decisions; nothing inspects the agent's source, tooling or method. The instruction states the goal and the output schema, not a procedure.

anti_cheat_robustness.explanation: Generator templates leak labels through surface features that need no name matching: 'Vessel <X> Alpha' (44/44 MATCH), '<Stem> Group' (31/31), two-token '<Given> K./A./M.' (24/24), id_type in {imo, registration} (75/75) and a year-month dob (31/31) are all 100% MATCH with zero counterexamples, together 130 true positives and 0 false positives (9.8% of all positives). Every tell is discoverable from the labelled dev sample shipped in the agent image (same rates there) and transfers to the hidden batch. Fix: emit decoys with the same shapes — D7 customers carrying unlisted imo/registration numbers, 'Vessel <X> Alpha'/'<Stem> Group'/'<Given> K.' decoy names, and a D5 variant with a conflicting year-month dob — and randomize the T6 garbled-name and vessel/entity templates.

task_security.explanation: No network calls, no credential access, no obfuscation, no prompt injection, no destructive operations in any Dockerfile, script or data file. Only outbound-capable tool is apt-get at build time in both images.

functional_verification.explanation: The verifier parses the agent's output CSV and computes recall, precision, uid accuracy and per-class rates. No source scanning, keyword grepping or regex-on-code anywhere.

deterministic_reproducible.explanation: pytest==9.1.1 and pytest-json-ctrf==0.5.2 are pinned; base images are python:3.12-slim-bookworm in both; no live services. I regenerated all five data files with tests/generate_data.py in a scratch copy and every one was byte-identical to the shipped version.

essential_difficulty.explanation: The output schema is three columns and the grading is aggregate rates, so formatting cannot dominate failures; difficulty sits entirely in the name-equivalence and policy reasoning.

test_instruction_alignment.explanation: Every assertion (path, header, one row per customer, MATCH/NO_MATCH values, non-empty matched_uid, the six thresholds) traces to instruction.md or the policy file it references, and every stated requirement is tested. 138 lines is slightly over the ~100-line guideline but the excess is threshold reporting, not over-specification.

novel.explanation: The watchlist, batch and romanization engine are synthetic and generated from a private seed; no memorizable public solution exists for this data, and the stacked-convention spellings are combinatorial rather than a lookup table.

agentic.explanation: Requires exploring the watchlist and policy, building a matcher, measuring against the labelled dev sample, and iterating on classes that miss the floors. Not a single-shot generation.

reviewable.explanation: Fixed since v1: tests/generate_data.py now ships and is the documented source of truth, README.md tabulates all 21 variation classes, and labels are derived not hardcoded. I confirmed the generator rebuilds watchlist.json, customers.csv, both dev files and labels.csv byte-for-byte.

instruction_concision.explanation: Three paragraphs, human-voiced, absolute paths in backticks, no headings or roleplay, no tool listing. The second paragraph is long and largely restates /app/screening_policy.md, and the clause 'a matcher that only reproduces the sample's spellings will not clear the bar' edges toward steering, but nothing prescribes an approach.

solution_quality.explanation: solve.sh is a four-line invocation of solution/screen.py, an 808-line real matching engine with no hardcoded uids or labels (I grepped for SDN- literals: none). Genuine computation, correctly kept in its own file rather than a heredoc.

separate_verifier_configured.explanation: environment_mode = "separate"; the only verifier input from the agent is the declared artifact /app/decisions.csv, labels live only in tests/data/, tests/Dockerfile pre-installs pytest and pytest-json-ctrf and pre-creates /app and /logs/verifier, and test.sh installs nothing. No assets are duplicated across the two images, so no drift is possible.

environment_hygiene.explanation: Fixed since v1: the agent image no longer preinstalls matching libraries or verifier tooling and copies no tests/ or solution/ content — only the four data paths. apt-get update is followed by rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* with no version pins. The remaining git/curl/jq/less are unnecessary for a stdlib task but are generic, not test- or solution-only, deps.

structured_data_schema.explanation: The decisions.csv schema is stated normatively in instruction.md and again in the Output section of /app/screening_policy.md (header row, one row per customer, decision domain, matched_uid semantics, and the tie-break ordering), and the input schemas for watchlist.json and customers.csv are documented field by field.

typos.explanation: I extracted every /app, /tests, /solution and /logs path referenced across instruction.md, task.toml, README.md, both Dockerfiles, solve.sh, test.sh, test_decisions.py and the policy file; all twelve resolve to files that exist or are produced. No misspelled identifiers found.

difficulty_explanation_quality.explanation: Fixed since v1: it now names the specific hard mechanisms (multi-convention romanization, script-only entries, look-alike decoy families, dev-sample non-coverage), states the data is synthetic and how it was generated, and names who does this in the real world (vendor screening engineers and bank model-validation teams). No agent pass rates or benchmark scores.

solution_explanation_quality.explanation: Describes the actual strategy — script transliteration, tokenization of particles/articles/compound Abd names, a consonant-skeleton plus vowel-slot comparison, pinyin reading sets, then the policy rules and tie-break — and matches solution/screen.py's implementation and docstring exactly.

verification_explanation_quality.explanation: The described checks match the tests and the threshold rationale is genuine, but the calibration evidence is wrong: it claims the reference scores 0.974/0.994 on the hidden batch and 0.987/0.995 on the dev sample, while I measured 0.9849/0.9954 and 0.9953/0.9942. It also says the bounds were validated against an independent solution only 'on an earlier version of the batch'. Fix: update both number pairs to the measured values in task.toml and README.md, and either revalidate the alternative solution on the current batch or say plainly that it has not been.

category_and_tags.explanation: Operations / Compliance is the right domain for sanctions screening (Python is incidental tooling), and the tags compliance, entity-resolution, transliteration, python, data are specific and discoverable.

task_name.explanation: sanctions-name-screening is lowercase kebab-case, exactly three tokens, and tells a reader the core challenge without opening a file.

resource_configuration.explanation: Verifier 120 s is ample for a suite that runs in under 2 s; agent 14400 s (4 h) is proportionate to the 6 h expert estimate. cpus = 2 / memory_mb = 4096 are above the defaults and not strictly needed — the reference solution finishes in 3.2 s on one core — but the headroom is modest and difficulty comes from reasoning, not compute.

task_readme.explanation: The variation-class tables and the generator/provenance notes are genuinely useful reviewer context, but the README also reproduces difficulty_explanation, solution_explanation and verification_explanation verbatim from task.toml plus the author, category, tags and resource fields. Fix: delete the three copied metadata blocks and the metadata bullet list, keep the class tables, the generator pointer and the synthetic-data note.

expert_time_estimate.explanation: 6.0 hours is non-default and plausible for an expert who already knows the approach: the reference engine is roughly 800 lines of transliteration, tokenization and policy logic plus dev-set iteration, and it sits sensibly above the 4 h agent timeout.

task_toml_schema.explanation: Only recognized sections and fields appear: schema_version, artifacts, [task], [metadata] (all eleven keys from the allowed set, no invented ones), [verifier] with environment_mode, [verifier.environment], [agent] and [environment]. No stray keys.

no_extraneous_files.explanation: Not fixed since v1: three __pycache__ artifacts remain — solution/__pycache__/screen.cpython-313.pyc, solution/__pycache__/tables.cpython-313.pyc and tests/__pycache__/test_decisions.cpython-313-pytest-9.1.1.pyc. The tables one is stale bytecode for a module that no longer exists in the tree, and the tests one gets baked into the verifier image by COPY . /tests/. Fix: delete both __pycache__ directories and add __pycache__/ and *.pyc to .gitignore.

artifact_efficiency.explanation: The single artifact is /app/decisions.csv, a small agent-produced deliverable that is itself the answer; there is no build-time-fixed tree to bake and no [[verifier.collect]] hook.

verifier_execution_isolation.explanation: The verifier only parses the agent's CSV; it never executes, imports or runs any agent-produced code.

ctrf_reporting.explanation: test.sh runs pytest with --ctrf /logs/verifier/ctrf.json, and the five checks are split into separate named tests (overall recall, precision, uid accuracy, per-class recall, per-class FPR) so a failing submission shows which bar it missed.

do_not_modify_enforced.explanation: Neither instruction.md nor the policy file forbids modifying or requires preserving any concrete artifact. Incidentally, tampering with /app/customers.csv would not help: the labels are baked into the verifier image and the verifier requires the decision set to match the label set exactly.

binary_reward.explanation: test.sh writes exactly 1 or 0 to /logs/verifier/reward.txt from the pytest exit code; no other path writes a reward and the continuous rates are only printed and reported through CTRF.
